### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. microspherophakia and/or megalocornea, with ectopia lentis and with or without secondary glaucoma  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.787)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:6715)

**Proposed mechanism:** LTBP2 (HGNC:6715) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Ectopia lentis (HP:0001043); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Microspherophakia (HP:0000514); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Megalocornea (HP:0000515); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Secondary glaucoma (HP:0000501). Loss-of-function mutations in LTBP2 disrupt extracellular matrix organization, leading to ocular developmental abnormalities such as ectopia lentis, microspherophakia, megalocornea, and secondary glaucoma.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of individuals with pathogenic LTBP2 variants exhibiting normal ocular development and absence of these phenotypes would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Pathogenic variants in LTBP2 with an allele frequency > 0.01% in gnomAD would suggest incomplete penetrance or a different underlying mechanism.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the role of LTBP2 in extracellular matrix organization and ocular development could lead to targeted therapies for these rare eye conditions, potentially involving strategies to support or restore ECM integrity.

#### 5. inflammatory bowel disease, immunodeficiency, and encephalopathy  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.398)

**Proposed mechanism:** Variant in LTBP2 (HGVS:unknown) —DISRUPTS→ LTBP2 (HGNC:6904); LTBP2 (HGNC:6904) —DECREASES→ Extracellular Matrix Remodeling (GO:0030198); Extracellular Matrix Remodeling (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormality of connective tissue (HP:0003547); Variant in TGFB1 (HGVS:unknown) —DISRUPTS→ TGFB1 (HGNC:11724); TGFB1 (HGNC:11724) —DECREASES→ TGFB1 signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-162777); TGFB1 signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-162777) —LEADS_TO→ Inflammatory Bowel Disease (HP:0002726); TGFB1 signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-162777) —LEADS_TO→ Immunodeficiency (HP:0002705); TGFB1 signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-162777) —LEADS_TO→ Encephalopathy (HP:0001291). Mutations in TGFB1 dysregulate the TGFB1 signaling pathway, which impacts both immune regulation and neurological function, leading to IBD, immunodeficiency, and encephalopathy (Disease B). The convergence is on the TGFB1 signaling pathway, as LTBP2 is known to interact with and modulate TGF-beta signaling components, suggesting a shared mechanistic node.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of any evidence linking LTBP2 or its protein product to the modulation of TGF-beta signaling or its downstream effectors would falsify this hypothesis. **Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of TGF-beta signaling in these distinct rare diseases could reveal common therapeutic targets. Modulating TGF-beta signaling might offer a therapeutic strategy for both conditions, potentially addressing immune dysregulation and tissue integrity.
